subject: Cloud marketplace purchasing pathways — billing, entitlements & legal Q&A
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@alphasys.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Miguel Duarte <miguel.duarte@alphasys.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Marketplace procurement questions ahead of PO

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement at AlphaSys is preparing a short questionnaire for how Redwood expects to be purchased when we go through cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP). High level asks from our side:

- How will billing occur if we buy through AWS Marketplace private offers vs direct Redwood invoice?
- Do you support meter-based usage reporting or only monthly invoice/seat?
- What legal flow is required for a private offer (DocuSign vs marketplace contract)?
- Any differences in indemnities / data residency commitments if purchased via marketplace listing?

We pasted a small set of follow-ups here and attached a 1-page checklist. Can you confirm who at Redwood owns marketplace listing vs commercial terms so we can loop them in?

Best,
Olivia Chen
Head of Procurement, AlphaSys

Attachment: AlphaSys_Marketplace_Checklist.pdf (PDF)
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@alphasys.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement questions ahead of PO

Hi Olivia —

Appreciate the thoughtful list. Looping in Kar (commercial ops) and Laura (legal & contracts). See inline responses below and I attached a short consolidated Q&A in case you want to circulate to your Sourcing/Cloud teams.

1) Billing flow: both options supported.
   - AWS/Azure/GCP private offer: Purchases route through the cloud marketplace billing pipeline (your org invoice from Amazon/Microsoft/Google). Redwood receives a settlement from the marketplace; we reconcile monthly.
   - Direct invoice: standard Redwood monthly invoice (Net 30/Net 45 depending on contract).

2) Metering: we support both per-token metering via marketplace metering APIs (where available) and subscription/commit billing. Metering requires integration/registration of the product with the marketplace meter service; it does add a ~1 billing-period reconciliation lag for usage-based charges.

3) Private offer legal flow: marketplaces typically allow private offers that reference a seller-provided contract (DocuSign) or accept the marketplace’s standard contract. For AlphaSys we can do a private offer referencing Redwood’s signed agreement (preferred) or accept AWS contract terms where required.

4) Indemnities / data residency: functionally no difference in product capabilities. Legal terms can vary slightly—if purchased via the marketplace seller contract, we can include the same indemnities and data residency clauses as our direct contract. If the marketplace forces its standard terms, we’ll surface any deviations.

Action items:
- Laura: see attached draft private offer language; confirm any non-starters for AlphaSys to present to legal.
- Kar: can you confirm whether Redwood can enable marketplace metering for this prospect and timeline to enable?

I attached: Redwood_Marketplace_QA_Responses_v1.pdf and Draft_Private_Offer_Terms.docx

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@alphasys.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement questions ahead of PO

Olivia —

Quick legal note after reviewing Jon’s draft:

- Indemnities: Redwood will accept mutual IP indemnities typical for SaaS. We cannot accept open-ended third-party product indemnities (we'll use carve-outs).
- Data residency / processing: we can commit to AWS region-specific data storage for the hosted product under Private deployment or Dedicated customers; for hosted accounts via marketplace we can add a data residency addendum where feasible.
- Subprocessors / KMS: we will provide subprocessors list and support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; marketplace purchases using hosted tenants will have standard cloud provider KMS handling unless a private deployment is requested.
- Audit requests: SOC 2 reports can be shared under NDA; for marketplace transactions we will coordinate with your security contact on redaction.

Non-starters: broad indemnity or export-control indemnity beyond US/EU law.

I can turn the draft into redlines if you share AlphaSys legal’s preferred clause-by-clause notes. If you’d prefer, we can do a 30-min walk-through with your counsel next week.

—Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@alphasys.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement questions ahead of PO

Hi Olivia —

Operational notes from Marketplace/Ops perspective:

- Metering enablement: For AWS Marketplace we can enable metering within 7-14 business days after the private offer is initiated. Metering will report SKU-level usage; please confirm which product SKUs AlphaSys wants metered (hosted-api, embeddings, dedicated-hourly).
- Settlement cadence: AWS settles monthly to Redwood with a ~45-day lag; this is something procurement should be aware of for cashflow.
- Private offer flow: after Redwood uploads the private offer to the AWS console, AlphaSys accepts it from their Marketplace console; the private offer can reference a Redwood DocuSign agreement or rely on AWS contract.
- Billing line items: we can include detailed line items (SKU, units, effective rates) to match your internal chargeback model.

Next step: please confirm SKU list + desired billing model (metered vs committed) and whether you want Redwood to initiate the private offer or if AlphaSys prefers to raise the private offer request.

Thanks,
Kar
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. Couple quick confirmations for our SFDC record and our legal team: 

- AlphaSys will request a private offer referencing Redwood’s DocuSign agreement (preferred).
- Billing model: start with subscription/commit for the first 12 months and add metering for embeddings after Q1 2027.
- SKUs to include: hosted-api-monthly, embeddings-per-1M, dedicated-gpu-hour.
- Legal: Miguel will upload redline comments on a shared DocuSign packet late tomorrow; Laura, can you accept a redline session on 2026-12-03 at 10:00am PST?

We will expect the private offer invitation from Redwood after your confirmation. If possible, please include the approximate settlement lag note in the PO so Finance can plan.

Olivia
Head of Procurement, AlphaSys Inc.
